Slope is a good starting point. A derivative is a slope, but it's a slightly special one.

Take $f(x) = x^2$. The slope of a line through two points is easy to find. At $x = 3$, though, there's only one point to work with. A single point doesn't give you a slope.

How would you use the limits you already know to turn "slope between two points" into "slope at one point"?
